summary: Dispatched the measurement that answers why the origin's decided index never advances, after a local run that also corrects the wording of my last counterevidence. The separation case now reports what the origin itself believes at the sample point, and locally it reports `origin_promise_pid` 3 with `origin_phase_accept` true while its decided index is still 0 — so the origin was re-prepared and re-synchronised (its promise moved and it entered the accept phase, which only happens through an `AcceptSync`) and its decided index stayed 0 because that `AcceptSync` carried decided index 0, the new leader itself having decided nothing. That contradicts the sentence I recorded last turn, that the scenario does not exercise a completed re-synchronisation at all: it does, and the re-synchronisation simply carries no decided progress. The shift still appears (returned index 4 while entry 33 sits at index 2), so the defect account stands; what changes is the explanation of the phase field, now measured rather than inferred. The submitted case is a revision adding those two read-only measurements with the scenario, poll flag, tick period and comparison unchanged. Incomplete: that receipt is pending; why the new leader never decides its own entry in this construction remains the open item, since that is what would give the receipts a re-synchronisation that both completes and carries progress.
